question: Can a cheap metadata-only model trained on direct terminal interventions predict held-out omitted-slab terminal value materially better than the existing local residual score?

training_set.labels: the 168 equal-byte force/eviction terminal-KL deltas under r25f/r31f plus the previously measured E586:R0 and E769:R11 arms

heldout_set.fixture: Implement a Python function that parses JSON and returns sorted unique keys.

estimator.name: terminal-marginal metadata ridge
estimator.target: equal-byte terminal KL recovered by forcing the omitted slab into local Budget24
estimator.standardization: fit mean and population standard deviation on the discovery training rows only; leave one-hot columns unscaled
estimator.fit: closed-form L2 ridge with an unpenalized intercept
estimator.lambda_selection: maximum mean Spearman under leave-one-route-out discovery cross-validation; ties choose the larger lambda

conditional_validation.procedure: Starting from held-out local Budget24, test predictor-ranked omitted candidates in measured one-swap order, then conditionally test 2 and 4 simultaneous swaps against the weakest measured selected/drop members. Do not infer additivity from independent marginals.
conditional_validation.bytes: must remain exactly Budget24 sidecar bytes with unchanged exact-fallback bytes
conditional_validation.selection_leakage: The held-out marginal labels may score the preregistered ranking and identify the measured weakest selected controls, but may not refit the estimator.

decision.go: Use the estimator as a cheap candidate generator on additional held-out layers, then test actual equal-byte terminal KL.
decision.no_go: Archive the negative result. Do not add metadata-model complexity. Move to a small terminal group-intervention or downstream-gradient estimator and compare it against the same held-out screen.

limitations: This is a cheap empirical baseline, not Fisher, Hessian, JVP, or causal attribution by itself.
Passing one prompt-transfer gate would not establish cross-layer or model-wide reliability.
Rank correlation alone cannot promote a selector; actual equal-byte KL and top1 are mandatory.
